title: October West Coast Family Adventure: Glaciers, Pancake Rocks & More
meta_desc: Discover October on NZ's West Coast with kids 5+. Get weather tips, top free walks, budget-friendly stays, booking advice and practical family hacks for a wild yet relaxed holiday.
intro: October is spring on the West Coast, when waterfalls roar and the glaciers still hold winter snow. Families can enjoy iconic sights without the summer crowds, and most activities are free or low‑cost. Here’s a practical guide to make the most of your October road‑trip.

sections.heading: Weather, Daylight & Packing
sections.body:
Spring on the West Coast brings mild days (average 14‑19 °C) and occasional rain showers – the region’s rain‑forest thrives in October. Expect 7‑8 hours of daylight, giving plenty of time for short walks and beach stops.

Pack layers: a waterproof jacket, fleece, sun hat and sturdy shoes for river walks. Sunscreen is still essential – the UV index can reach 6 on clear days.
list: Sturdy walking shoes (good grip for glacier walkways)
Thermal base layer for early morning glacier visits
Sun hat, sunglasses and SPF 30+ sunscreen

sections.heading: Top October Activities (5+ years)
sections.body:
October’s cooler temperatures make the short glacier walks comfortable, and the waterfalls along the West Coast are at their peak. All the listed walks are free and suitable for kids aged 5 and up.

Start at Punakaiki (30‑minute walk to the Pancake Rocks), then head south to Hokitika Gorge – a 25‑minute drive from town and a 20‑minute easy river walk. The glacier valleys at Franz Josef and Fox are just 3 km return walks from the car parks, with interpretive signs that keep children engaged.
list: Punakaiki Pancake Rocks & Blowholes – free, 30 min walk, 1h30 drive from Hokitika
Hokitika Gorge turquoise river walk – free, 20 min loop, 25 min from Hokitika
Franz Josef Glacier valley walk – free, 3 km return, 2h drive from Hokitika
Fox Glacier viewing platform – free, 2 km return, 30 min from Franz Josef

sections.heading: Booking Ahead & Crowd Levels
sections.body:
October is shoulder season, so most attractions are uncrowded, but accommodation in popular towns (Hokitika, Franz Josef) can fill quickly, especially long‑weekend stays. Book your holiday home or cabin at least 3 weeks in advance.

Reserve a table at the Wild Foods Café in Hokitika if you want the kid‑friendly greenstone carving demo – they only take 10 groups a day.
list: Airbnb or Holiday Parks – 2‑bedroom cabin $180‑$220 per night (incl. kitchen)
Wild Foods Café – $25 adult lunch, $12 child (pre‑book via phone)
Petrol – $2.30/L (budget $30‑$40 per day for a 600 km loop)

sections.heading: Sample Daily Budget (Family of 4)
sections.body: Below is a realistic day‑by‑day cost guide that stays within the $150‑$250 daily budget. Fuel, meals and accommodation are the biggest items; all walks and most sights are free.

rows: Lunch – Wild Foods Café (2 adults, 2 kids)
Optional activity – Guided glow‑worm walk (Franz Josef)

sections.heading: Practical Family Tips for October
sections.body: Traveling with kids on the West Coast can be a breeze if you plan for the weather and keep the schedule flexible. Here are five tried‑and‑tested tips.
list: Start each day early – the morning light makes the gorge water vivid and reduces the chance of rain.
Keep a “rain kit” in the car: zip‑lock bags for wet clothes, extra socks and a thermos of hot chocolate.
Use the free public toilets at the DOC sites – they’re clean and have baby changing facilities.
Buy fresh fruit and sandwiches at Hokitika’s Saturday market (open 8‑12 am) for cheap, kid‑friendly picnics.
Let the kids collect “rock passports” – a small notebook to stamp at each free site (Pancake Rocks, Gorge, Glacier).
